title: Web Request Containing Suspicious JNDI Parameters - Potential CVE-2021-44228 Exploit (Log4Shell)
desc:
Identifies patters of JNDI usage that are related to the Log4Shell exploit. These strings can be found in any header field that is logged by a vulnerable server (utilizing a vulnerable version of Log4j). These field should appear in proxy, web server, database or similar logging sources that utilize the Log4j logging package. NOTE -- Several data sources are provided, however if possible the strings provided should be queried across all data sources, including cloud logging (such as Azure or AWS) in addition to DNS and database logging. This is due to the currently unknown impact across vendors and products. Additionally, if possible, utilize the provided hunts that use regex to capture applicable strings. This regex, as of December 18th, have been verified against over 10K strings observed in the wild to properly capture all known variations of the exploit string with minimal potential for unintended results.

title: ShadowCopy Image Accessed
desc:
This package is intended to help identify when Shadow Copies are accessed on a user's host. This can be the cause of creating a new backup, setting up Shadow Copies, restoring from old backups or due to malicious access to normally protected files. In July 2021 a privilege configuration issue was identified, enabling access to NTLM hashes and other sensitive data that is typically protected with SYSTEM level access on the normal filesystem. This vulnerability is tracked as CVE-2021-36934 and dubbed SeriousSAM or HiveNightmare. The vulnerability affects access to The C:\Windows\System32\config\ folder, containing the SYSTEM, SAM and SECURITY hive files. Typically these files are protected to only SYSTEM level processes, however they can be accessed utilizing Shadow Copies that fail to protect it the same as in the original source folder.

desc:

Based on research, the method of utilizing "Bypass" is more common in malicious executions, however "Unrestricted" should still be monitored for abuse, such as insider threats. The included flags and parameters in the query logic search for potentially malicious activities that may deviate from standard practices within a specific environment. desc:

They are often utilized for legitimate purposes, however when utilized maliciously the key name/value is often obviously suspicious, such as random names, or objects loaded from temp or public folders.

desc:

Some general suggestions may be to group by parent processes to identify common, approved and legitimate, applications; group by common line and only review command lines observed less than 3 times, across 3 hosts (indicating single execution across multiple hosts); or limit the results by distinct number of hosts and event counts, such as limiting to less than 5 observed hosts or total execution count.

title: LSASS Memory Dumping using WerFault.exe - Command Identification
desc:
This use case is meant to identify WerFault.exe (Windows Error Reporting) creating a memory dump of lsass.exe (Local Security Authority Subsystem Service, a process responsible for the enforcement of security policies on Windows systems, which generates and stores credentials in its process memory). This is accomplished by using a mechanism called "Silent Process Exit", which can allow for specific actions to occur when the process terminates itself or if another process terminates it. For this specific method, the action will be modified to create a memory dump file of the process terminated - in this case lsass.exe.

desc:

This Hunt Package is intended to identify other executions of Microsoft Word with "-Embedding" in the command line parameters, indicating it was opened from another application. This is consistent with how "background" execution via COM services is performed when exploiting Microsoft Word. Most recently this was theorized from a vulnerability in Microsoft Outlook (CVE-2024-21413).

title: Suspicious File Extension Executed From INetCache - Potential Malicious File Executed From Remote Host
desc:
Attackers can utilize malicious WebDAV servers to host files that will execute remotely from a compromised host. When a file is retrieved and subsequently executed via a WebDAV share, a copy of the file is temporarily stored in `AppData\Local\Microsoft\Windows\INetCache`. This technique can be utilized via malicious links clicked on by the user, or by the attacker post compromise as a method to easily execute their malware across multiple devices without the need to move the malware from system to system. This can be achieved via commands such as `rundll32.exe \\10.10.1.1\webDAV\share\safe.dll,EntryPoint1`. In February of 2024, the vulnerability tracked as CVE-2024-21412 was unearthed by Trend Micro as a result of analysis from a DarkCasino (Water Hydra) attack. This vulnerability abuses Internet Shortcuts to chain multiple shortcuts together to eventually bypass Defender SmartScreen, which notifies users when a file may be malicious to execute. The last step of the observed attack bypassed the path applied for CVE-2023-36025, which was also a SmartScreen bypass. This technique is quite creative as the user is tricked into executing a malicious Internet Shortcut from a WebDAV share after clicking on a link. The attacker did this by making the pop-up window that follows the link appear to be the user's downloads, where its actually the attacker controlled WebDAV share. Once the user clicked on the malicious Internet Shortcut, another Internet Shortcut was retrieved, which pointed to a malicious .cmd file located within a .zip file on the WebDAV share.

title: Microsoft Message Queuing (MSMQ) Feature Service Created/Started - Potential Running Vulnerable Service
desc:
This Hunt Package was developed in response to a critical vulnerability (CVE-2024-30080) identified in the Microsoft Message Queuing Service (MSMQ). This vulnerability could lead to a Remote Code Execution (RCE) condition on any host with the MSMQ service enabled. The provided query logic is designed to identify when the MSMQ Service is started or registered on a target system. The existence of a Create Service or Service Start event is indicative the target device is running the MSMQ Service. While MSMQ is a Windows component that facilitates asynchronous communication by sending and receiving messages, its activation, particularly if not typical in your environment, can be a red flag. This service is widely used for legitimate purposes, but it can also be exploited by threat actors for malicious activities, such as executing arbitrary code, escalating privileges, or disrupting services.

title: Excessive Occurrences of 1 in Command Line - Potential Malware Command Obfuscation
desc:
At least two ransomware strains have been found to utilize a method to execute their commands utilizing a specific number of 1 digits as the command line argument instead of the real parameters. This makes it appear as though a command is executed with varying number of 1s as parameters and effectively obfuscates what the malware is attempting to execute. This method effectively evades detection mechanisms and doesn't naturally appear malicious. However, the malware executes the new command with the process in a suspended state, then changes the parameters in memory and continues the command. Due to how monitoring and logging operates, defense mechanisms and logging tools will not be able to capture the modification of the command post execution. Because of this, the command line parameters are effectively invisible to logs. Fortunately for threat hunting this makes easy use of looking for an excessive number of consecutive 1s, which should be abnormal beyond 3-5 digits (could be an IP or host designator).

title: Direct to IP Address in Execution of WebDav DLL via Rundll32 - Malicious Link or Exploitation
desc:
This Hunt Package focuses on identifying attempts by attackers to coax Microsoft applications, LOLB or similar applications to utilize WebDav to communicate over HTTP to attacker controlled infrastructure. In recent reports, attackers have exclusively utilized direct to IP communication for their WebDAV addresses. As such, the provided query syntax looks for the composition of an IP structured like a UNC path within the execution of rundll32 to create a WebDAV session. This activity has been observed in several vulnerabilities, such as CVE-2023-22397, CVE-2023-36025 and CVE-2024-21412. Web Distributed Authoring and Versioning (WebDav) is an extension of the HTTP protocol that allows users to collaboratively edit and manage files on remote web servers. In typical use, WebDav provides a convenient means for file sharing and collaboration. WebDav can be abused by adversaries to execute arbitrary code and perform other malicious activities, such as specially crafted links in websites and phishing emails, and Internet Shortcuts.

title: DLL and EXE File Written in Same Directory in Short Period - Potential DLL Write for DLL Side Loading
desc:
This Hunt Package aims to identify potential DLL side-loading activity by searching for when an executable and a small number of DLL files are written to the same directory within a short period of time. This type of activity could be indicative of an attacker attempting to load a malicious DLL by abusing a legitimate application that would normally load a safe DLL file from the same folder its installed to. Attackers abuse this functionality to load a malicious DLL by the same name as the legitimate DLL the program is normally expecting. Additionally, this technique helps obfuscate the attacker's initial DLL execution by masking a potentially malicious name and instead masquerading as a legitimate DLL name when observed in execution logs.

title: Command Obfuscation Attempt - Windows Shell Escape Characters Found in cmd.exe Execution
desc:
Detects the use of escape (^) characters on the commandline for cmd.exe. This method is used in obfuscation attempts to try and break string matches. An excessive number of escape characters on the command line of the Windows Shell is uncommon in benign applications. It is, however, an effective string-breaking technique used to bypass security applications that rely on matching particular strings or regex structures, and proper application of string escapes can provide layers of obfuscation that will endure in log sources without impacting the usability of the command. This technique has been abused by malicious actors in the wild, incorporated into aggressor tools for Red Teams, and was a partial subject of FireEye's DOSfuscation report.

title: Abnormal Execution of WebDav DLL via Rundll32 - Potentially Malicious Link or Exploitation
desc:
This Hunt Package focuses on identifying attempts by attackers to coax Microsoft applications, LOLB or similar applications to utilize WebDav to communicate over HTTP to attacker controlled infrastructure. In March 2023, Microsoft issued a patch for the vulnerability tracked as CVE-2023-23397, which was a critical EoP vulnerability in Microsoft Outlook that is triggered when an attacker sends an appointment with an extended MAPI property with a UNC path to an SMB (TCP 445) share on a threat actor-controlled server. In addition to SMB, it was found ports and services could be forced, such as WebDav over SSL:443 or HTTP:80. Web Distributed Authoring and Versioning (WebDav) is an extension of the HTTP protocol that allows users to collaboratively edit and manage files on remote web servers. In typical use, WebDav provides a convenient means for file sharing and collaboration. WebDav can be abused by adversaries to execute arbitrary code and perform other malicious activities. In this particular case, attackers may send malicious calendar invites or appointments, which trigger the "reminder notification" sound for the proposed meeting or event. As a result, Outlook will initiate a connection to the configured address found in the "PidLidReminderFileParameter" appointment MAPI field.

title: 3CX VoIP Desktop Application Parent to Itself - Suspicious Process Chain Indicative of Supply Chain Attack
desc:
This Hunt Package is intended to identify when the 3CX VoIP Desktop Application is a parent of itself in a windows environment. This has been reported by several security vendors and researchers when installing the compromised version of the software. This execution chain occurs when a ICO file is downloaded from a GitHub page that contains malicious Base64 data. This parent/child relationship should be uncommon in most instances of the application. **IMPORTANT** Based on current information available as it relates to the reported Supply Chain Attack by `LABYRINTH CHOLLIMA`, the affected versions noted thus far are `18.12.407` and `18.12.416` for Windows. According to 3CX's [Build History](https://www.3cx.com/blog/change-log/web-client-desktop-app/), these versions were introduced in March of 2023. Furthermore according to [Huntress](https://www.huntress.com/blog/3cx-voip-software-compromise-supply-chain-threats), there appears to be a 7 day "sleep" based on their analysis. As such, analysts should focus their efforts on process executions in March 2023 as a priority to identify the known compromise activity. Once this has been performed, additional searches and analysis can be performed to expand scope into other builds that may be affected and not yet reported. It is important to note, based on feedback from vendors, researchers and 3CX it appears the issue originated from an upstream package utilized by 3CX, which limits even further the potential scope for older builds being affected. More information is being released as researchers and vendors are performing analysis and mitigations. Information will be updated as quickly as possible, but please bear in mind this is a developing story and details provided are based on industry research, lab analysis and feedback from the community and therefore may present small inaccuracies.

title: AdvancedRun/InstallUtil Utilities Executed From Unusual Directory
desc:
Microsoft Windows Utilities are almost exclusively utilized from their native directories, often in C:\Windows\System32\, however in some cases attackers copy the tool into a directory of their choosing and utilize it for various follow on actions. This package was initially developed in response to the WhisperGate attack against the Ukrainian government in January 2022. In this attack the WhisperGate malware dropped AdvancedRun.exe to the host's temp directory, and copied InstallUtil.exe from it's default location to AppData\Local\Temp. In the case of InstallUtil.exe, the malware utilized this for process hallowing to have a legitimate appearing binary running malicious code injected by WhisperGate. The AdvancedRun.exe utility was utilized by WhisperGate to further impair Windows Defender beyond the path exclusions added by a VBS file.

title: Suspicious File Extension Written to INetCache - Potential Malicious File Downloaded From Remote Host
desc:
Attackers can utilize malicious WebDAV servers to host files that will execute remotely from a compromised host. When a file is retrieved and subsequently executed via a WebDAV share, a copy of the file is temporarily stored in AppData\Local\Microsoft\Windows\INetCache. This technique can be utilized via malicious links clicked on by the user, or by the attacker post-compromise as a method to easily execute their malware across multiple devices without the need to move the malware from system to system. This can be achieved via commands such as rundll32.exe \10.10.1.1\webDAV\share\safe.dll,EntryPoint1. In February of 2024, the vulnerability tracked as CVE-2024-21412 was unearthed by Trend Micro as a result of analysis from a DarkCasino (Water Hydra) attack. This vulnerability abuses Internet Shortcuts to chain multiple shortcuts together to eventually bypass Defender SmartScreen, which notifies users when a file may be malicious to execute. The last step of the observed attack bypassed the path applied for CVE-2023-36025, which was also a SmartScreen bypass. This technique is quite creative as the user is tricked into executing a malicious Internet Shortcut from a WebDAV share after clicking on a link. The attacker did this by making the pop-up window that follows the link appear to be the user's downloads, where it's actually the attacker-controlled WebDAV share. Once the user clicked on the malicious Internet Shortcut, another Internet Shortcut was retrieved, which pointed to a malicious .cmd file located within a .zip file on the WebDAV share. Additionally, this detection also covers CVE-2024-29988, a vulnerability related to WebDAV requests in web browsers, which complements our understanding of evolving threats.

title: Uniquely Named Driver Writes With FileNames Between 4-10 Characters
desc:
The intent of the provided query logic is to identify when an environmentally unique driver name has been written to the Windows default drivers directory that ranges between 4 and 10 characters in length. This is a behavior of the Terminator malware that utilizes a "Bring Your Own Driver" type of attack by shipping a vulnerable driver with their malware package to run commands or carry out operations at the kernel level. As reported by a CrowdStrike engineer on Reddit, the Terminator malware will drop a vulnerable driver (such as the reported signed Zemana anti-malware kernel driver) and will name it a random string between 4 and 10 characters within the windows default driver folder. This technique allows the attacker to run kernel level activities via the driver.

title: Potential Fake Browser JavaScript Execution - Likely User Executed
desc:
Manually executed JavaScript files can be indicative of a social engineering attack, such as phishing, where the user is coaxed into opening a JavaScript file from their downloads, or temporary folders, such as Internet Temporary Files. JavaScript executions are not inherently malicious, however when the JavaScript files or paths contain common browser names, and are launched by the default application wscript (often attackers utilize more stealthy methods such as rundll32.exe), it can be an indication the user was victim of a fake browser update/install attack. This package identifies when a JavaScript file (extension) is originally launched from Downloads, Temp or AppData directories, is indicative of user execution (OpenWith.exe or explorer.exe) and is then executed by wscript.exe, where the filename or directory of the target JavaScript contains common browser names in the folder path or file name.

title: Suspicious OneNote Exported File in Command Execution - Potential OneNote Phishing
desc:
This hunt package aims to identify potential OneNote phishing activity involving suspicious extensions that are commonly abused to run malware on a Windows system. Emotet, a banking Trojan, is now being distributed via Microsoft OneNote email attachments in an attempt to bypass macro-based security restrictions and compromise systems. The attackers use social engineering techniques to entice victims into enabling macros to activate the attack chain. The OneNote file is simple but effective in social engineering users with a fake notification stating that the document is protected. When instructed to double-click on the View button, victims inadvertently double-click on an embedded script file instead. The Windows Script File (WSF) is then engineered to retrieve and execute the Emotet binary payload from a remote server.

title: Java Writing WAR File - Potential Exploitation of Web Service
desc:
This Hunt Package was developed in response to an Apache Struts vulnerability tracked as CVE-2023-50164. During exploitation of this vulnerability an attacker can utilize the file upload function of Apache Struts to load a .war file to a desired directory via a path traversal bug. In publicly available Proof of Concepts the path observed was '/op/tomcat/webapps', however, based on the application and its underlying web service, this path may be different. The attacker then uploads a .war file which is ingested by the web service and unpacked into a web application. The new web application would contain the malicious package the attacker wanted to upload for access, most likely a webshell. During research of the applicable vulnerability it was noted that Java would be the most likely culprit of the file upload on the affected system. Although .war files may be legitimately deployed via the upload webapp, its often not a standard practice and all .war files should be scrutinized. NOTE: If no events are identified from your initial hunt execution, the manual Validation steps MUST be run on a test system with a 'Gold Image' type setup to ensure the applicable folders are monitored by the security tool. During research and development it was noted that not all EDRs will log the .war file creation specifically in '/opt/tomcat/webapps', however its possible the EDR will log other directories applicable to your specific deployment of web services.

desc:

The vulnerability recently garnered attention due to the Follina vulnerability, as it operates in a similar fashion by abusing HTML files to load malicious code via MSDT. Specially crafted diagcab files can be utilized to download malicious programs and save them on the target host. The provided query logic is designed to identify when MSDT executes a diagcab file or executes the command that will retrieve the malicious target file to download and store on the victim host.

title: UAC Bypass Attempt - User Interface Privilege Isolation (UIPI)
desc:
This use case is meant to identify when a User Interface Privilege Isolation (UIPI) bypass method is attempted. User Interface Privilege Isolation (UIPI) implements restrictions in the Windows subsystem that prevent lower-privilege applications from sending messages or installing hooks in higher-privilege processes, however higher-privilege applications are permitted to send messages to lower-privilege processes. To bypass these UIPI restrictions, an application that is digitally signed and trusted by the host, installed in a secure location (such as C:\Windows), and contains 'UIAccess="true"' in its manifest, is capable of interacting with other programs interfaces without requiring elevation (an example is Osk.exe, On Screen Keyboard, which can be started by non privileged users and interact with other programs). This functionality can ultimately be abused to bypass User Account Controls and execute applications at a higher privilege level than otherwise achievable.

desc:

The uniqueness of the child process can be an indication of unexpected activity being performed by Java, potentially by an exploit. The provided query is designed to return all java process executions, and therefore will return legitimate results. This is intended to catch the unknown child processes that may be unique to the attacker or target. The query will sort by uniqueness first and if supported by the tool, will limit unique counts returned, to help identify outliers. This package was originally inspired by the Log4Shell, Spring4Shell, and Text4Shell vulnerabilities released in late 2021 and 2022, respectively.

title: Rundll32 executing inf file - Potential CVE-2021-40444 Activity
desc:
Microsoft Word suffered from a ZeroDay attack in September 2021, tracked as CVE-2021-40444. The vulnerability allowed code execution by Microsoft Word without the need of a macro to run. A amlicious Word document containing this exploit would allow the attacker to reach out to a website under their control, download and execute a payload, all without user interaction after the document is opened. Once the vulnerability is carried out the control.exe process will be utilized several times in order to locate a INF file, which will then be executed by rundll32. The INF is actually a DLL file and early stages of analysis of the exploit reveal it cannot be guaranteed where it will be dropped post exploitation. This is why the control.exe process is spawned several times in order to locate it and execute it.

title: Microsoft Outlook Communicating Over Unusual Ports - Potential Exploitation
desc:
This Hunt Package was originally generated in response to a critical vulnerability in Microsoft Outlook, tracked as CVE-2024-21413. In addition to this vulnerability, this Hunt Package identifies potentially suspect network activities over port 80 or 445. While Outlook may generate a normal request over port 80, singular requests can often be an indication of malice. In February 2024, a zero-day was announced in Microsoft Outlook, tracked as CVE-2024-21413. The vulnerability enables attackers to obtain NTLM hashes from targeted users. Additionally in some cases a remote code execution scenario can occur without user interaction after a malicious link is clicked inside an email. The malicious email will likely appear like a typical phishing email, however instead of prompting a user to ensure they want to open the link, it bypasses this security check and automatically downloads and opens the attacker controlled file. Initial POCs that surfaced after the vulnerability disclosure, utilized SMB shares, external to the target machine to host files for the malicious link to download/execute. It is important to note, at the time of this Hunt Package's creation, it is unclear the extent of applications or file types that can be abused as part of this vulnerability. As such, aside from mshta, other likely suspicious applications have been included to provide a more complete picture if the vulnerability expands.

title: Microsoft Office Applications Network Communication Over Suspicious Ports - Potential Exploitation Attempt
desc:
This Hunt Package is designed to identify outbound HTTP activity from Microsoft Office applications over suspicious ports that are uncommon to normal network activities associated with Office. These ports include 445/139 for SMB related activities and TCP Port 80, which is clear-text HTTP. Most communications will be SSL encrypted via HTTPS, except potentially OPTIONS requests and other atypical requests. Additionally, Microsoft Office products should not communicate over SMB protocols unless Macros are written to directly do so, which may be common in some environments. These two protocols can be indicative of a recent zero-day vulnerability affecting Microsoft Office products, tracked as CVE-2023-36884.

title: Excessive Empty Doublequotes on Cmdline for Cmd.exe
desc:
Looks for more than one instance of empty doublequotes ("") on the commandline. This method is used in obfuscation attempts to try and break string matches. An excessive number of escape characters on the command line of the Windows Shell is uncommon in benign applications. It is, however, an effective string-breaking technique used to bypass security applications that rely on matching particular strings or regex structures, and proper application of string escapes can provide layers of obfuscation that will endure in log sources without impacting the useability of the command. This technique has been abused by malicious actors in the wild, incorporated into aggressor tools for Red Teams, and was a partial subject of FireEye's DOSfuscation report.

title: Suspicious Rundll32 Execution - Non-DLL File Execution With Suspect Entry Points
desc:
Rundll32 is utilized to load and execute modules or functions of DLL files, but is often abused to execute binary files. The provided package focuses on identifying two suspicious entry points invoked in a binary file (non-dll) by Rundll32. DllRegisterServer entry point is often called during registration of a DLL file on the system, but can be used as a defense evasion technique to hide as a legitimate entry point call. An additional suspect entry point is Control_RunDLL. This entry point is legitimately utilized as a method to call control panel items, often requiring a .cpl file in addition to the .dll file. These two entry points are often abused by malware and exploits, such as Emotet, QakBot (QBot) and CVE-40444, as a method to get malicious code running on a system.

title: Suspicious HTA File Writes - Potential Exploitation or Social Engineering
desc:
HTML Application (HTA) files can be utilized by attackers to trick users into executing malicious code. The intent of this Hunt Package is to identify when a HTA file is downloaded/written to a folder path that can be indicative of malicious code. This Hunt Package was originally generated in response to CVE-2024-348112, in which HTA code is cached by Internet Explorer (even with Edge/Chrome installed and set to default browser), in IE's INetCache folder in the user's AppData\Local directory. In a recent campaign, reported by CheckPoint, an adversary utilized a new zero-day, tracked as CVE-2024-38112, to trick users into downloading a malicious HTA file from a remote server and executing WMI and Powershell commands to deliver an infostealer malware. In this new campaign the attacker convinces a user to download and execute a crafted .url file. This specially crafted URL file, containing code to exploit CVE-2024-38112, is programmed with a link to a web page hosting HTA code. The vulnerability works by utilizing two special flags in the "URL="" field of the URL file: "mhtml:" and "!x-usc:". When these modifiers are utilized correctly, it enables a URL file to download and execute HTA code. In the observed infostealer campaign, the attacker concealed their HTA code by making the download and execution of the URL file a PDF file. In the attack chain, a fake window is opened with PDF like text to think the user did indeed download a PDF file, while the infostealer malware runs in the background.

title: Microsoft Message Queuing (MSMQ) Feature Service Enabled - Potential Vulnerable Service Creation
desc:
This Hunt Package was developed in response to a critical vulnerability (CVE-2024-30080) identified in the Microsoft Message Queuing Service (MSMQ). This vulnerability could lead to a Remote Code Execution (RCE) condition on any host with the MSMQ service enabled. The provided query logic is designed to identify when the MSMQ service is enabled (accompanying service is created in Microsoft Services Panel) on a target system, via the registry keys that are generated when the service is enabled on a Windows host. While MSMQ is a Windows component that facilitates asynchronous communication by sending and receiving messages, its activation, particularly if not typical in your environment, can be a red flag. This service is widely used for legitimate purposes, but it can also be exploited by threat actors for malicious activities, such as executing arbitrary code, escalating privileges, or disrupting services.

title: Local Service Executing Abnormal Process - Potential Exploitation or LPE
desc:
In February 2024, Microsoft provided a patch for a LPE vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2024-21338, enabling an attacker to perform read/write directly to the Windows kernel. The vulnerability was originally classified as an "admin-to-kernel" vulnerability, however it was found the "Local Service" account was required as either a starting point or intermediary account to carry out a successful exploit. Due to the requirement of the "Local Service" account, the malicious process associated with the attack, such as the staging malware, initial access malware or backdoor, would have to either impersonate or elevate their privileges to this account. One of the available Proof of Concepts for this vulnerability only required the "attacker" to have administrative privileges before impersonating Local Service, and eventually elevating to SYSTEM and allowing kernel level read/write. NOTE: VPN Clients will utilize the LOCAL SERVICE account for various tasks. Ensure to identify approved VPN clients and exclude them from the Hunt.

title: Suspicious Child Process to Microsoft Outlook - Potential Outlook Exploitation or Suspicious Script Execution
desc:
This Hunt Package was originally created in response to a critical vulnerability in Outlook, tracked as CVE-2024-21413. In February 2024, a zero-day was announced in Microsoft Outlook, tracked as CVE-2024-21413. The vulnerability enables attackers to obtain NTLM hashes from targeted users. Additionally in some cases a remote code execution scenario can occur without user interaction after a malicious link is clicked inside an email. The malicious email will likely appear like a typical phishing email, however instead of prompting a user to ensure they want to open the link, it bypasses this security check and automatically downloads and opens the attacker controlled file. It is important to note, at the time of this Hunt Package's creation, it is unclear the extent of applications or file types that can be abused as part of this vulnerability. As such, aside from mshta, other likely suspicious applications have been included to provide a more complete picture if the vulnerability expands.

title: Compressed Files or Scripts Written to wwwroot Directory - Potential Webshell Staging Artifacts or Exfiltration
desc:
This hunt is designed to identify potential artifacts staged by an attacker utilizing a webshell. The provided logic focuses on common extensions of compressed files and other commonly observed extensions utilized for data collection, such as powershell scripts and batch files. Except during installation of a new web server, occurrence of these files should typically be uncommon for the wwwroot folder. In common web server installations files are written to a web server's wwwroot directory under separate folders based on function, location, or other grouping mechanism to make managing the files on the web server easier. The presence of these files types in the wwwroot directory can be indicative of a webshell that has already been loaded to the web server and the attacker is loading tools or staging data for exfiltration. This Hunt Package was originally created to help identify instances of MoveIT exploitation related to the vulnerability tracked as CVE-2023-34362.

title: Web User Account Creation, Login and File Creation for Same User in Cisco IOS - Potential Exploitation and WebShell Upload
desc:
This Hunt Package focuses on when a web user account is created, followed by an account login, followed by a file creation event within 2 minutes to a Cisco IOS device. Analysts can look for common malicious accounts like those containing the word "cisco", "support" or "admin" and validate each account creation returned for the hunt. This activity is often associated with exploitation and webshell upload, where the attacker is able to create an account via a vulnerability and then load their payload onto the target device via the newly created account.
